chunks: I heard al-Ridha (peace be upon him) saying:
'A friend of every person is his intellect, and his enemy is his ignorance.'

key_terms.جَهْل: Ignorance (jahl) — the opposite of 'aql, representing spiritual and moral blindness.
key_terms.عَقْل: Intellect or reason ('aql) — in Shia theology, a faculty given by God that enables one to discern right from wrong and know God.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about intellect and ignorance in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) teaches that a person's intellect ('aql) is their truest companion and ally, while ignorance (jahl) is their greatest adversary. This aphorism reflects the central Shia theological emphasis on reason and knowledge as divine gifts essential for spiritual and moral progress. The saying was transmitted through a reliable chain and spoken directly to al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, one of the Imam's close companions in Khurasan.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm who said, 
‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘
A friend of every person is his intellect, and ‘عَدُوُّهُ جَهْلُهُ’ his enemy is his ignorance’.
